chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding a waterflow of the valley of Mahzour that the upper part should withhold upon the lower part, for the palm tree up to the (level of) the two ankles, and for the cultivation up to the two shoe-straps.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on water retention for upstream agricultural users?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records the Prophet Muhammad’s (SAWW) judicial ruling in the valley of Mahzur, establishing the principle of upstream retention to ensure equitable water distribution for downstream users. It specifies precise physical benchmarks for this retention—up to the ankles for date palms and up to the shoe straps for grain crops—reflecting the practical agricultural norms of 7th-century Arabia. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on preventing the waste of resources (israf) and securing the rights of neighbors in communal water usage.
